name: OpenCode

surfaces.label: OpenCode v1 desktop app (1.x, Electron). Matched on the utility helper that hosts the server, NOT on the main app process: the main process has Chromium helper children that would always look like tool children. Prod bundle id ai.opencode.desktop; beta and dev channels append .beta / .dev (their app names contain a space, which the probe's space-splitting cannot match by path). The v2 desktop (2.x, same bundle id) has no NodeService helper at all: it runs the bundled CLI as a background service, see the last daemon surface.

opencode in a terminal (default command, also `opencode attach <url>`; also the VS Code/Cursor extension terminal, which adds --port). Native Bun-compiled binary named `opencode`; the npm package installs it as bin/opencode.exe. v1 (1.x): agent and server run in a Worker thread of this process, so tree signals on it are meaningful. v2 (2.x, @opencode/cli): this process is a thin client of a shared background service (`opencode serve --service`, see the daemon surface), so its own tree_cpu and tool_children read idle while a turn runs. The name `opencode` is also the archived Go project's binary, installed to the same ~/.opencode/bin path (false positive, see notes).

opencode serve / opencode web: headless HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:4096 by default (v1), `web` also opens a browser. In v2 the same match catches `opencode serve --service`, the detached background service every v2 CLI and desktop client shares (default port 49374 = 0xc0de, registration file ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json); it outlives the TUI and serves all sessions, so its tool children cannot be attributed to one session. Loose match: args_contain is a substring test, so a project path containing 'serve' or 'web' also matches.

opencode run <message>: non-interactive one-shot. The process lives for exactly one prompt, so existing implies working (inferred; no listed signal encodes it), unless it is `run --attach`, where the work happens in the remote server. Loose match: the probe splits ps args on spaces, so a prompt or path containing the words run, serve or web is mistaken for a subcommand.
opencode acp: Agent Client Protocol server over stdio, spawned by an editor such as Zed

OpenCode v2 desktop (2.x): the app runs its bundled CLI as the background service. Packaged builds copy Contents/Resources/opencode-cli to <userData>/cli/<version>/opencode-cli, i.e. under ~/Library/Application Support/<app>/, and spawn `<that> serve --service` detached. There is no Electron utility helper. The path contains a space, and the probe splits ps args on spaces, so the executable name cannot be matched: this surface matches the exe prefix /Library/Application plus the arguments opencode-cli and --service, which are both required. Same shared service as the CLI's `serve --service` above.

working_signals.meaning: The bash tool spawns one detached child shell per command, so a child that is not an LSP or MCP server means a tool call is running. Caveat: LSP servers and stdio MCP servers are long-lived children while idle, so this over-reports. Meaningful on the v1 TUI/serve/run surfaces and on the v1 desktop utility helper. For v2 the tools are children of the shared `serve --service` process, not of the TUI or desktop app, and that process serves every session, so a hit says only that some session runs a tool.

Inferred, not measured: the TUI animates a spinner while a session is busy and the model stream is parsed in-process. No opencode process was available to calibrate the floor. Does not apply to a v2 TUI or the v2 desktop app: the model stream is parsed in the shared service process.

waiting_signals.meaning: A tool needs approval (bash is 'ask' in the plan agent, and any 'ask' rule). Cleared by permission.replied. session.status stays 'busy' the whole time, so busy does not mean working.
The model called the question tool and waits for an answer. Cleared by question.replied or question.rejected. Source-only: not in the docs event list.

Pending requests on a server you can reach: opencode serve/web, or a TUI started with --port/--hostname. Add ?directory=<cwd> or header x-opencode-directory. A plain TUI has no listening port, and the desktop app's server password is random per launch.
Optional sound and terminal notification on question, permission, error and done. Off by default. Not readable from outside.

v2 only, source-level (packages/protocol/openapi.json, tag v2.0.19), not exercised. /api/session/active returns {data:{<sessionID>:{type:'running'}}} and 'sessions absent from the result are inactive', the precise turn signal. /api/permission/request lists pending permission requests. The service URL, pid and password are in ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json (XDG_STATE_HOME/opencode/service.json), which `Service.discover` reads with the same user's rights. Basic auth, user 'opencode'.

hooks.config: No shell-command hook config. Lifecycle handlers are JS/TS plugins: ~/.config/opencode/plugins/ (global), .opencode/plugins/ (project), or the `plugin` array of npm packages in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c) or project opencode.json. The `event` hook receives every bus event.

telemetry.how: Undocumented, source-only. Set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (optional OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS as k=v,k=v and OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES): OTLP over HTTP, traces to <endpoint>/v1/traces and logs to <endpoint>/v1/logs, no metrics. Resource service.name=opencode with opencode.client (cli or desktop), opencode.run and service.instance.id. Nothing is exported when the variable is unset. Separately, config experimental.openTelemetry=true turns on AI SDK spans (function id session.llm, session id in metadata). A GUI app does not see shell env, so the desktop app needs launchctl setenv or a launch from a shell. v2 (2.x): packages/cli/src/index.ts passes the same OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS to its own Observability.layer; span and log shape not checked.

sources.claim: TUI is one process: the server and agent run in a Bun Worker thread inside it. No listening socket unless --port, --hostname or --mdns is passed; otherwise the TUI talks to the worker through in-process RPC fetch on 'http://opencode.internal'.
sources.evidence: packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui.ts: 'const worker = new Worker(file, ...)', 'const external = hasArg("--port") || hasArg("--hostname") || network.mdns === true', 'url: "http://opencode.internal", fetch: createWorkerFetch(client)'. Docs (https://opencode.ai/docs/server) say the TUI 'randomly assigns a port', which the source contradicts.

sources.claim: A process cannot be mapped to its session by argv. Only -s/--session <id> carries an id, and only on resume; -c/--continue carries none. Otherwise map by working directory (lsof cwd) to session.directory in the DB, newest time_updated, parent_id IS NULL. All v1 processes on the latest, beta and prod channels and the v1 desktop app share one database; a dev-channel build uses opencode-dev.db. In v2 the sessions are in table session_v2 of the same opencode.db file (see the v2 store source).

sources.claim: Message text deltas are not persisted, only published on the event bus; the DB is written when a part or message is created or finishes. So DB writes stall during a long model stream, and the shared -wal file mtime cannot say which session wrote.

sources.claim: The precise in-process 'turn in progress' state is session status busy | retry | idle, set busy when a run starts and idle when it ends. Events session.status and (deprecated) session.idle. Exposed by GET /session/status (per directory) and the /event and /global/event SSE streams. GET /session/status returns only sessions that are busy or retrying: set(idle) deletes the entry, list() returns the map, the handler returns Object.fromEntries(list()). An idle session is absent, not reported as idle.

sources.claim: v2 architecture: the CLI TUI is a thin client. `opencode` resolves a shared background service (ServerConnection.resolve -> Service.ensure), starting it if missing by spawning `<self> serve --service` detached and unref'd; the service default port is 0xc0de (49374) for channels latest/dev/beta/next; the registration file is <XDG_STATE_HOME or ~/.local/state>/opencode/service.json with url, pid, version and a private password. `--standalone` runs an in-process server instead; `--server <url>` attaches to a remote one. Flags -c/--continue and -s/--session are kept. Subcommands new in v2: api, mini, pair, reload, service (serve gains --service).

notes: Two product lines with different shapes; treat them separately. V1 (1.x, opencode-ai, what opencode.ai/install and brew give today). (1) Terminal: one native process named `opencode` (npm installs it as `opencode.exe`), agent and server in a Worker thread, no socket unless --port. From outside it exposes no turn flag: use tool_children (noisy, LSP/MCP children) and CPU. If it was started with --port/--hostname (VS Code extension, `opencode attach` targets, serve, web), GET /session/status?directory=<cwd> returns a map of sessions that are busy or retrying; an idle session is absent from it. (2) Desktop: Electron app ai.opencode.desktop; the server is a utility helper (--utility-sub-type=node.mojom.NodeService) with a random port and per-launch password, so its status API is not reachable from outside. Match that helper, not the main process. V2 (2.x, @opencode/cli and the 2.x desktop, released 2026-09, docs banner 'OpenCode v2 is now available'). The TUI and the desktop app are both thin clients of one detached background service, `<opencode or opencode-cli> serve --service`, that serves every session and outlives them. The TUI process and the desktop main process do no agent work, so tree_cpu and tool_children on them read idle; the work shows in the service process and cannot be attributed to a session by process tree. Precise signals exist (GET /api/session/active, GET /api/permission/request) at the URL and password in ~/.local/state/opencode/service.json, but this is source-level only and was not exercised. Sessions live in table session_v2 of the same opencode.db. The v2 plugin/hook API, event names and OTLP payloads were NOT checked; the hooks and telemetry fields describe v1. Common: busy also covers 'waiting for permission'; use permission.asked / question.asked (plugin event or SSE) to see the human wait. Map a process to a session by cwd against ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (v1 table session, v2 table session_v2; session.directory, newest time_updated, parent_id IS NULL), unless -s was given. The DB is shared by every process and the desktop app, so file mtime cannot attribute activity. Open the DB read-only; it is WAL. Known false positives and misses of the process patterns: (a) the archived Go opencode-ai/opencode is also named `opencode` and installs to the same ~/.opencode/bin, so it matches the tui surface; nothing in ps separates them; (b) the probe splits ps args on spaces, so a prompt or path containing the exact word run, serve or web changes the surface, and a project path containing serve or web matches the loose daemon surfaces; (c) the v2 desktop service path contains 'Application Support', so it is matched by the /Library/Application prefix plus args opencode-cli and --service, which is a workaround and untested against a real process; (d) beta and dev desktop apps contain a space in the app name and are not matched. Not verified live: no OpenCode process or install exists on this Mac; every pattern was tested only against made-up ps lines, so confidence stays documented at most, and the CPU floor and working signals are inferred.
